verdict.rationale: Nix's own docs say `nix-shell` builds or downloads a project's declared dependencies and starts a shell with all required environment variables set. `nix develop` does the same for a derivation's build environment. A hands-on community report confirms `nix-shell --run` reliably ensures a team has all the correct dependencies, matching the one-command bootstrap of a fresh clone. Missing for 10: the documented steps assume Nix is already installed (a separate curl installer step), and there is no explicit evidence of a lockfile-pinned fresh-clone workflow (e.g. flake.lock).

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: the command `nix-shell` will build or download those dependencies if they’re not already in your Nix store, and then start a Bash shell in which all necessary environment variables (such as compiler search paths) are set.
`nix develop` - run a bash shell that provides the build environment of a derivation
Nix is extremely useful for developers as it makes it easy to automatically set up the build environment for a package.
you can do `nix-shell --run "<some command>"`, and it will make sure you have all of the correct dependencies.
